Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: No evidence found of formal independent security reviews of Sudan's national ID system. Sudan scored Tier 4 (48.17/100) on the Global Cybersecurity Index in 2024, reflecting limited cybersecurity maturity. The Sudanese Cybersecurity Authority was established in late 2025 but no documented security audit or review of the ID system specifically was found in research.

revision_notes: Initial light check (single search) surfaced a clearly authoritative primary source, so this row was escalated from the fast path to full verification rather than confirmed as Unknown. A press statement from the Sudanese Cybersecurity Authority (SCA), corroborated by state news agency SUNA (via sudanakhbar.com) and reported by Sudan Events on 29 May 2026, states that the Sudapas national digital identity platform 'undergoes regular security reviews and testing' to ensure readiness and strengthen cybersecurity protection; the SCA's official website (sca.gov.sd) confirms it is the genuine government cybersecurity regulator and lists auditing/compliance assessment among its services. Score changed from 0 (Unknown) to 2 (Yes) on the scale 0=Unknown; 1=No; 2=Yes. Note this is a self-reported/internal claim by the system's own regulatory bodies rather than a documented independent third-party audit; flagged for human review to confirm whether an independent audit exists, given the claim's recency (platform launched 21 May 2026) and self-reported nature.
revised_comments: Sudan's national digital identity platform, Sudapas, is reported by the Sudanese Cybersecurity Authority to undergo regular security reviews and testing to ensure operational readiness and strengthen cybersecurity protection. Encryption key management and digital certificates for the platform are administered by the National Authority for Digital Authentication under approved security controls. These are internal reviews conducted by the system's own regulatory bodies; no independent third-party audit has been publicly documented.
